chapter: Tulsa bands, Trent, Holder and Kirk
title: Wiring a duplex and working for Spot and Tate Electric
summary: He wires a duplex without a license, a Black electrical contractor firm inspects it and hires him; the tape side ends.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Anyway, I was with this marching band, but I came on over to Tulsa and met some Tuskegee (inaudible), and one of them--two carpenters, they were a lot older than me, they were about my brother's age, and they were doing quite a bit of work, and when I told them I was a Tuskegee grad, they said yeah, and so a guy from the western part of Tulsa was building duplex apartments and he told them that he wanted that wired and so I told him okay and I did the wiring.
He said, have you had it inspected; I said inspected? I said no. He said you have

to be inspected before you can turn the electricity on. He said, I didn't question you because I figured you knew what you were doing, but you have to have a license (inaudible) and he said, now, are you sure it's all right. So I said so far it is (inaudible), but I said it's wired okay and everything.

So he said okay then, I'll get Spot and Tate to have it inspected for you, and have them come out and look it over, and so that was a colored electrical contractor then, Spot and Tate Electric Company. So they came out and looked it over and they said, that's pretty good, you got a little change in the box, but everything else is all right (inaudible), and they asked me how I got the job--they went to school where I came from--so they said, do you want a job and I said sure, and they said you can work for us.
Spot was one man's name and Tate was the other; Spot and Tate Electric.
Before I make a change in the tape, could you still do electrical work, can you still do it?
(Side A of Tape 1 ended at this point. Transcript will continue in accordance with Side B.)
